content.text:
`0.html` was already in good shape, so I made only three small additions to the stylesheet. I haven't opened it in a browser to check them.

- **List indent:** `ul`, `ol` and `menu` now indent 1.5rem instead of the browser default 40px, matching the existing `dd` indent.
- **Table headers:** `thead th` aligns to the bottom, so short headers sit on the rule when a neighbouring header wraps.
- **Print:** `abbr[title]` now prints its expansion in parentheses, the same way the external link URLs already do.

Three things I left alone:

- **Content:** the page is still just a title and an `<h1>` of "0", with no `<meta name="description">`. I didn't invent any text.
- **Tables:** `table { display: block }` gives horizontal scrolling without wrapper markup, but can cost table semantics in some screen readers. The fix is a wrapper element around each table, which is a markup change.
- **Headings:** `h4`, `h5` and `h6` all render at the same size (1rem bold). That only matters if you nest headings that deep.
